introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: 5. (a) Using the outline map of Cameroon provided, show the main vegetation types of Cameroon. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method.** On the outline map draw approximate boundaries, shade or colour each vegetation belt, label it and add a key and a title. The belts follow the rainfall gradient and run roughly east-west across the country.

**Vegetation types (from south to north).**
1. *Mangrove* in a narrow strip along the Atlantic coast and the estuaries (Douala, Limbe, Kribi areas).
2. *Equatorial (evergreen) rainforest* in the south (the South, Centre, East and coastal regions, up to about 5 degrees N).
3. *Forest-savanna mosaic* (the transition) between the forest and the savanna, roughly 5 to 6 degrees N, including the Western Highlands and the Adamawa fringe.
4. *Montane (highland) vegetation and grassland* on the Western Highlands and the volcanic mountains (for example Mount Cameroon, Mount Oku).
5. *Guinea (wooded) savanna* on the Adamawa Plateau, roughly 6 to 8 degrees N.
6. *Sudan savanna* in the Benue basin and the northern plains, roughly 8 to 10 degrees N.
7. *Sahel (Sudano-Sahelian) steppe* with thorny scrub in the Far North, north of about 10 degrees N, as far as Lake Chad.

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2020-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_2.png)

**Marking guide.** Four marks: at least four vegetation belts placed correctly 2, labels or shading 1, key and title 1. Approximate boundaries are accepted.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Describe the main natural and man-made tourist resources of Cameroon. *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon, called "Africa in miniature", has a great variety of tourist attractions; at this level examples must be named and located.

**Natural resources (about 5 marks).**
- *Relief and volcanoes:* Mount Cameroon (over 4,000 m, an active volcano in the south-west, with an annual race and hiking), the crater lakes of the Western Highlands (for example Lake Nyos, Lake Oku, Barombi Mbo), the Mandara Mountains with the rock towers near Rhumsiki, and the Western Highlands (Bamenda, Bamenda Ring Road) with a cool climate and scenery.
- *Coast and beaches:* the black volcanic beaches of Limbe and the white sand beaches of Kribi, with the Lobe Falls plunging into the Atlantic Ocean; the Ekom-Nkam waterfalls in the Moungo area.
- *National parks, game and forest reserves:* Waza National Park in the Far North and the Benoue National Park in the North (savanna game such as elephants, giraffes and lions), the Korup National Park and Dja Faunal Reserve (rainforest, primates and birds), the Campo Ma'an park.
- *Lakes and rivers:* Lake Chad and the Logone, and the Sanaga and the lagoons for fishing and boating.
- *Climate and vegetation:* sunshine and the variety of landscapes from rainforest to savanna and semi-desert.

**Man-made (cultural) resources (about 5 marks).**
- *Traditional palaces and museums:* the Sultan's palace and museum in Foumban (Bamoun), the Bafut palace in the North West, and the Lamidates of the North (Rey Bouba).
- *Gardens, zoos and sanctuaries:* the Limbe Botanic Garden and the Limbe Wildlife Centre, the Mefou primate sanctuary near Yaounde, and the Mvog Betsi zoo.
- *Festivals and handicrafts:* the Ngondo festival of the Sawa people in Douala, the Nguon festival of the Bamoun, craft markets (Foumban, Bamenda) with bronze, wood carving and weaving.
- *Monuments and modern facilities:* the Reunification Monument in Yaounde, hotels and resorts (for example at Kribi, Limbe, Yaounde), international airports at Douala and Yaounde and the road and rail links.

**Marking guide.** 5 marks for named and located natural resources, 5 for man-made ones; reward a balanced answer with examples.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Explain three socio-economic impacts of the tourist industry in Cameroon. *(9 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three impacts, each stated and developed for 3 marks. Both benefits and costs are acceptable.
1. *Employment and income (benefit):* tourism creates direct jobs (hotel, guides, drivers, park rangers) and indirect jobs (farming, crafts, transport, restaurants), which raises incomes and reduces rural-urban drift, for example around Limbe, Kribi and Waza.
2. *Foreign exchange and government revenue (benefit):* tourists bring foreign currency and pay park fees, visas and taxes; the state uses these to finance services; the multiplier effect stimulates local crafts and farming.
3. *Infrastructure and regional development (benefit):* roads, airports, electricity, water and telecommunications are improved for tourism and are used by the local population; towns grow, with new services.
4. *Cultural and social costs:* the commercialisation of local festivals and traditions, loss of cultural identity, crime and the pressure on local services and on land and housing prices.
5. *Environmental costs:* pollution and damage to ecosystems from the pressure of visitors, which can in turn reduce the resources on which tourism depends.

**Marking guide.** Three well explained impacts, 3 marks each; a statement alone earns 1 mark.
